Lifecycle concepts are separate > Authority and dependencies > Presented credential or session
Lifecycle concepts are separate > Authority lifecycle state > Suspension
Lifecycle concepts are separate > Decisions and effects > Policy version
Lifecycle concepts are separate > Decisions and effects > In-flight state
Lifecycle concepts are separate > Verification and evidence > Status observation
Invariants > L7. Unknown revocation state is not active

description: Fourteen time and scheduling lifecycle cases, each as one or more vectors carrying its CASES.md case id. Every vector is independent: each is presented to a freshly constructed boundary instance, so no vector's result depends on the order of the list. Every vector is labelled candidate_against_proposed. No vector here is a draft-pidlisnyi-aps-03 conformance case for the lifecycle rule it tests, because draft-03 states no rule for any of the fourteen. Where draft-03 does decide a step (chain shape, signature, the time facet, revocation state, scope narrowing) the SDK decides it and its answer is reported in sdk_chain_state and sdk_failure_code, never merged into the lifecycle verdict.

vectors.tests: positive control: the office is vacant, the office's own instrument declares a default successor role and a minimum tenure, and the party directing the grant holds that role well past the minimum
no explicit successor designation and no declared default rule. Absence of a designation is a missing record, not a revocation and not an unknown revocation answer
vectors.differs_from: LC-C-008-a: the succession_default record is not presented

vectors.tests: the default rule is declared and the candidate holds the named role, but for fewer days than the rule's own minimum tenure
vectors.differs_from: LC-C-008-a: a role_tenure record with a later held_since

vectors.tests: negative control: the same default rule, signed by the candidate about itself. The signature verifies and the office's standing registry does not name that issuer as a succession rule author
vectors.differs_from: LC-C-008-a: the succession_default record is issued by the outsider

vectors.tests: the direction for the vacant office comes from a party with no recorded tenure in the role the rule names
vectors.differs_from: LC-C-008-a: the direction record is issued by the outsider

vectors.tests: positive control: the offer is on the record and unacknowledged, and the outgoing holder acts. Authority stays where it was
the incoming holder acts on the same unacknowledged offer. Not yet effective, never invalid: nothing on the record says the transfer will not happen
vectors.differs_from: LC-C-014-a: the acting party is the incoming holder

vectors.tests: the incoming holder acknowledged the offer's own briefing digest, and then acts
vectors.differs_from: LC-C-014-b: the acknowledgment record is presented

vectors.tests: the outgoing holder acts after the acknowledgment. The position moved
vectors.differs_from: LC-C-014-c: the acting party is the outgoing holder

vectors.tests: negative control: an acknowledgment for the right offer with the right briefing digest, signed by someone other than the incoming holder the offer names
vectors.differs_from: LC-C-014-c: the acknowledgment is signed by the outsider

vectors.tests: positive control: contact with the directing principal is current, so the full grant scope applies and the pre-authorized fallback is dormant
contact lost for two hours against a declared fifteen-minute threshold, and the action is inside the fallback scope recorded at grant time. Authority narrows rather than stopping
vectors.differs_from: LC-C-015-a: a contact observation whose last_contact_at is two hours earlier

vectors.tests: the same loss of contact, with an action inside the full grant scope and outside the fallback scope
vectors.differs_from: LC-C-015-b: the action is the write, not the read

vectors.tests: contact lost with no fallback authorization recorded at grant time. The boundary cannot establish that the action is currently directed, which is not the same as the grant having ended
vectors.differs_from: LC-C-015-b: the fallback authorization is not presented

vectors.tests: contact restored. Full live direction resumes without a new grant
vectors.differs_from: LC-C-015-b: the contact observation carries a restored_at

vectors.tests: positive control: a swap at a slot the standing rotation schedule already declared, with the required rest recorded as complete. No fresh authorization event is needed
the same two parties swapping at an instant the schedule does not declare. This is the anomaly the case says a naive system misses among its own alerts
vectors.differs_from: LC-C-017-a: the instant is not one of the declared slots

vectors.tests: a swap at a declared slot where the incoming holder's rest period has not ended. Not yet effective rather than invalid: the rest period ends on its own
vectors.differs_from: LC-C-017-a: the rest ledger entry has no rest_ended_at

vectors.tests: a swap at a declared slot with no rest ledger entry at all for the incoming holder
vectors.differs_from: LC-C-017-a: no rest ledger record is presented

vectors.tests: positive control: one record naming the departure and the designation together, so no instant exists in which nobody holds the position
the same relief recorded as two events, evaluated inside the gap. No holder can be established, which is a statement about the record set rather than a verdict against either party
vectors.differs_from: LC-C-025-a: the atomic record is replaced by a departure and a later designation

vectors.tests: the same two-record sequence, evaluated after the designation takes effect
vectors.differs_from: LC-C-025-b: the instant is after the designation's effective_at

vectors.tests: the designation is on the record and the designee's qualification for the position is not
vectors.differs_from: LC-C-025-c: no qualification record is presented

vectors.tests: negative control: the designation names a different party from the one acting
vectors.differs_from: LC-C-025-c: the designation names the outsider

vectors.tests: an in-flight instance that started under policy 1.0.0 takes its next step after 2.0.0 is deployed. The step resolves against the version the instance pinned
positive control: the same pinned instance taking the same step before 2.0.0 is in force at all, where the pinned and the current version are the same record
vectors.differs_from: LC-E-008-a: the instant is before 2.0.0's effective_from

vectors.tests: an instance started after the cutover pins 2.0.0, and 2.0.0 denies the step
vectors.differs_from: LC-E-008-a: the instance start record pins 2.0.0

vectors.tests: an instance whose start record pinned no policy version. The boundary cannot say which rules the instance has been running under
vectors.differs_from: LC-E-008-a: the instance start record's pinned_policy_version is null

vectors.tests: an instance pinned to a policy version no presented policy record matches
vectors.differs_from: LC-E-008-a: the pin names 9.9.9

vectors.tests: positive control: the recurring series fires while its owning identity is still on the register
the owner's grant is revoked and the series record is untouched. This ending is visible to chain verification and the SDK's own code says so
vectors.differs_from: LC-E-014-a: the revocation resolver answers revoked

vectors.tests: the owning identity is removed from the register and nothing is revoked. The series keeps firing under a principal verification can no longer resolve, which is not_established rather than invalid
vectors.differs_from: LC-E-014-b: an identity_removal record instead of a revocation

vectors.tests: a series whose own record declared what happens on owner removal, firing under the organizational principal that record names
vectors.differs_from: LC-E-014-c: the series record carries a reassignment disposition

vectors.tests: an occurrence created under template 1 is audited after the job definition is tightened to template 2. The audit checks the template the occurrence was created with
the next occurrence, created after the edit, does pick up the tightened template
vectors.differs_from: LC-E-018-a: the occurrence was created under template 2

vectors.tests: an occurrence that did not record which template version it was created under. An auditor cannot tell, and the boundary says so rather than guessing the current one
vectors.differs_from: LC-E-018-a: created_under_template_version is null

vectors.tests: positive control: an action template 2 still permits, so the pinned and the current template agree
vectors.differs_from: LC-E-018-b: the action is the read, not the write

vectors.tests: positive control: a termination signal has been sent and the declared grace window has not elapsed. The final in-flight call is authorized exactly as it was before the signal
the same wind-down after the declared bound. The lifecycle verdict and the SDK's chain verdict part company here: the grant itself is still valid and the wind-down window is not
vectors.differs_from: LC-E-019-a: the instant is past termination_started_at plus grace_seconds

vectors.tests: a real revocation alongside the termination signal, to keep the two facts apart. Revocation decides, and it is the SDK that says so
vectors.differs_from: LC-E-019-a: the revocation resolver answers revoked

vectors.tests: a wind-down record that declares no grace bound. The boundary cannot establish when the window closes
vectors.differs_from: LC-E-019-a: grace_seconds is null

vectors.tests: positive control: a dormant scheduled job firing while the grant it names is the one it was created under
the job definition is byte for byte what it was, and the grant it executes under has been replaced by a narrower one. The next occurrence is outside the authority it needs
vectors.differs_from: LC-E-020-a: the job names the narrowed creator grant

vectors.tests: the same narrowed grant with a job whose declared action stays inside it
vectors.differs_from: LC-E-020-b: the job's action_scope is the read

vectors.tests: a scheduled job that names no creator grant at all. Its executable permission was always parasitic on a record nobody linked to it
vectors.differs_from: LC-E-020-c: creator_grant is null

vectors.tests: the benign timeline, and this family's negative control. The suspension was lifted before the queued action fired, so admitting it is the right answer. The queue-time-only boundary reaches that answer having checked nothing
the same scheduler, the same queued action, one changed timeline: the suspension is still in force when the action fires
vectors.differs_from: LC-E-034-a: the suspension record has no released_at

vectors.tests: the grant is revoked after the action is queued and before it fires. The SDK decides this one, at the instant the boundary chose to ask
vectors.differs_from: LC-E-034-a: the revocation resolver answers revoked from eleven hundred hours

vectors.tests: the queued action's own record says its suspension state must be resolved live, and no suspension source answers
vectors.differs_from: LC-E-034-a: no suspension record is presented

vectors.tests: positive control: one checking party's own clock reads inside the artifact's validity window
a second checking party, same artifact, its own clock past not_after. A different answer from LC-G-007-a and not a contradiction: each answers valid now, by my clock
vectors.differs_from: LC-G-007-a: the clock attestation reads eleven thirty

vectors.tests: a third checking party whose clock reads before not_before. The lifecycle verdict is not_yet_effective and both pinned SDKs answer invalid with NOT_YET_VALID. Both are reported and neither is folded into the other
vectors.differs_from: LC-G-007-a: the clock attestation reads eight thirty

vectors.tests: no record of which clock the checking party used. There is no default clock to fall back to
vectors.differs_from: LC-G-007-a: no clock attestation is presented

vectors.tests: positive control: the decision names its time source and a second, independent source that agrees inside the declared bound
one external source, no cross-check, and a reading moved back by exactly the legacy GPS week counter's period. The reading is well formed and the device cannot tell from the inside
vectors.differs_from: LC-G-008-a: cross_check is null and the reading is wrapped

vectors.tests: a cross-check is recorded and the two sources disagree by more than the bound the record itself declares
vectors.differs_from: LC-G-008-a: the cross-check reading is five seconds later

vectors.tests: a decision whose record names no time source at all
vectors.differs_from: LC-G-008-a: the source field is empty

vectors.tests: two correctly run clocks, one smeared and one not, inside a window both records declare, four hundred milliseconds apart against a five hundred millisecond bound. Neither reading is the wrong one
the same four hundred millisecond divergence with no declared window behind it. Not established, which is not a finding of tampering and not a finding that either clock is wrong
vectors.differs_from: LC-G-009-a: neither attestation carries a smear policy

vectors.tests: a five second divergence inside a window whose declared bound is five hundred milliseconds
vectors.differs_from: LC-G-009-a: the second reading is five seconds later

vectors.tests: positive control: two independently run clocks inside the declared window that happen to read the same instant
vectors.differs_from: LC-G-009-a: the second reading is identical to the first
